key_insight: PI-GINOT learns geometry-conditioned finite-strain hyperelastic responses directly from specimen shape, enabling data-free operator prediction for parametric DogBone mechanics.
engineering_relevance: This can replace many repeated finite-element runs in virtual testing, design optimization, and uncertainty studies when geometry varies.
method: Encodes each DogBone boundary point cloud into geometry features
Uses a cross-attention decoder to predict displacement at arbitrary interior points
Enforces boundary conditions and physics via autodiff, Neo-Hookean plane-stress constitutive laws, equilibrium, traction-free/symmetry, and internal-force consistency
evidence_signal: Validated only after training on eight unseen geometries with Abaqus, achieving 2.1%–7.1% displacement error, 0.9%–13.3% peak von Mises stress error, and section-force error below 10.3%.
watch_item: Local stress components can be inaccurate near the gauge-to-fillet transition, especially for narrow specimens where stress gradients are steep.
paper_title: PI-GINOT: Data-free geometry-informed neural operator learning for finite-strain hyperelasticity on parametric DogBone specimens
